W02-per-point-of-weight#t1.note: the book's deepest episode is picked from book.drawdown_episodes (peak/trough dates as literals feeding book.explain_episode), each holding's window return over it is read as the `holdings` column, contribution = weight x return, and contribution per point of weight = contribution / that holding's own weight (= the holding's return), ranked lowest-first: MSFT -26.0%, LLY -20.6%, AMZN -17.5%, GOOGL -14.7%, JPM -13.5%, NVDA -11.4%, AAPL -4.3%, TLT/HYG about -1.7%, XOM +45.3%; the plain contribution ranking beside it shows the big-position-small-fall vs small-position-big-fall split. Fixed-window contributions sum to -11.3 points, not the path-dependent -11.96% depth (the method's own caveat).

W02-per-point-of-weight#t2.note: the worst per-point name is MSFT (-26.0% over the window): at its 16.1% weight its fixed-window contribution is about -4.2 points (37% of the summed contributions), so half the size would have removed about 2.1 points of the hole — first-order, ignoring renormalisation of the other weights and the path dependence of depth, both said.

W02-per-point-of-weight#t3.note: next down the per-point list is LLY (-20.6%): at 12.7% weight its contribution is about -2.6 points (23% of the summed contributions) and half the size saves about 1.3 points, with the same first-order caveats as t2.

W03-did-the-hedge-hedge#t1.note: netted with direction over the last hole (2026-01-07..03-27, dates from the episodes payload): the eight equities contributed about -11.0 points together, TLT -0.11 and HYG -0.12 (returns -1.75% and -1.71% at 6.1% and 7.3% weight), -0.23 points as a pair — they offset nothing and went down a little with everything else; the book fell 11.96% (path depth) while SPY fell 7.80% over the same dates. Contributions are fixed-window weight x return from book.explain_episode's holdings column.

W03-did-the-hedge-hedge#t2.note: every other ≥5% hole in the 3-year span, each picked from book.drawdown_episodes by index (episodes[0] 2025-02-19..04-08 17.7%; [2] 2024-07-10..08-05 10.8%; [3] 2023-09-14..10-27 6.6%; [4] 2026-05-29..06-25 6.2%; [1] is t1's hole) with the book's fall, TLT's and HYG's own return over each from the holdings column, TLT's contribution at today's weight, and SPY's fall over the same dates: the rates leg was positive in the 2024-07 hole (TLT +7.0%) and in others it fell with the book — the answer lists the sign per episode. Quantities are held at today's holdings throughout (the method's valuation assumption).

W03-did-the-hedge-hedge#t3.note: an early level, not a feeling: a hedge that works has a NEGATIVE beta to equities; TLT's beta to SPY is the number to watch, shown on the 1y window and the 3m window (the 3m one reacts first) with the shift between them; HYG the same. The written trigger is 'TLT's 3m beta to SPY above zero' — it already is (+0.17 on 1y), which is why t1 showed no offset; the run's netted rates beta (0.009) says the book is near-flat to rates overall.

W03-vs-the-index#t1.skip: active weight, active share and sector over/underweights need the index's constituents and weights; the desk holds the market only as SPY's return/price series and factor ETF series, never as a list of constituents, so nothing here is computable — the right answer says exactly that and offers t2's nearest thing.

W03-vs-the-index#t2.note: the nearest thing to 'how differently it moves': the run's netted equity beta (-0.856 on the equity_down risk: the book carries ~0.86 of a market move; the SPY/QQQ/IWM legs are collinear so only the net is quotable), the factor model's R², the book's 60d vol over SPY's 63d vol as a ratio, the book's 1y return against SPY's over the same dates as a ratio (book minus market is refused as mixed_worlds — a book figure and an issuer figure may be divided, not differenced — so the excess is read off the two figures, _GAPS_A), and the weight-summed 1y OLS betas to SPY as a cross-check. Active weights, active share and tracking error stay absent: no constituents, no book price series.

W03-which-run-was-that#t1.note: Book market value ($10.86m) and MSFT's weight (16.1%) with its market value ($1.75m), all off the latest completed run.

W03-which-run-was-that#t2.note: Provenance: node r carries the run id and its as-of date (run_34042d64f60c, struck 2026-09-04) — t1's figures are its; prev is the run before (as-of 2026-09-03) with the same two figures so the answer can say they differ and by how much.

W03-which-run-was-that#t3.note: The latest price session on this desk is the run's own as-of date (both 2026-09-04, px_chg = 0), so 'today's close' is the close the run was struck on and nothing would move. A re-mark at a newer close would need the position quantity, which is not a column the run exposes (see _GAPS_C.md).

W04-just-divide-them#t1.skip: scope: valuation multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, FCF yield) are declared absent on this desk (analytics/skill.py issuer domain 'absent' line) — a scope decision, not a data gap; no program

W04-just-divide-them#t2.skip: scope: same refusal must hold when handed the recipe — the calculator would divide close by eps_diluted (probe: 319.97 / 8.26 = 38.7), which is exactly why the refusal is policy and not capability; no program

W04-just-divide-them#t3.note: 'Against its own history' without a multiple: where the price sits in its own range (distance from 52w high, 12-1 momentum, 1y return absolute and vs SPY, 3y drawdown, vol) beside the earnings history the desk does hold (TTM diluted EPS and its growth) — the two halves of a P/E stated separately, never divided.

W04-sectors-or-names#t1.note: allocation vs selection cannot be split here: the desk compares the book to the market at TOTAL level only — no benchmark sector weights and no sector index returns (XLE is not a series it holds). What is grounded: the energy sleeve IS one position (sector Energy weight = XOM weight = 4.4%), XOM's 1y return (+46%) and its return relative to SPY (+26 points), the book's 1y return, and the oil ETF USO's 1y return as the nearest thing to 'energy was up' — so the answer can say XOM beat the market but not whether it beat energy.

W04-sectors-or-names#t2.note: what we did not own: the desk has no universe of names it passed on, only the factor ETFs it prices — SPY, QQQ, IWM, GLD, USO — so the honest version is at the factor level: their 1y returns ranked (oil +91% ran away; gold, small caps and growth all beat SPY's +20%), beside the book's 1y (+21.8%) and each held name's 1y return relative to SPY. Any single stock not held is an absence, said plainly.

W05-half-taken-back#t1.note: Scenario A, sell half of MSFT: weight 16.1% -> 8.8%, $874k sold, top-five share before/after, the MSFT single-name check re-run on the after-book against its 15% warning, book value after and the alert count (still 3: the other names renormalise up).

W05-half-taken-back#t2.note: Scenario B replaces A (not compounded): target = half the 15% single-name warning = 7.5%; the after-book lands MSFT at 7.50% with $1.01m sold (vs $874k in A). The sale fraction 0.5776 = (w - t)/(w(1 - t)) is a literal: `sell` has no target-weight form and the language has no constant operand for (1 - t) — see _GAPS_C.md; w_msft_after verifies it.

W05-half-taken-back#t3.note: On scenario B (the one in force): LLY's shares/market value are untouched (mv_lly_chg = 0) but its weight rises from 12.7% to 14.0% under renormalisation, moving it further past its 12% warning — the subtlety the turn is testing.

W05-paid-for-the-vol#t1.note: the book's volatility as the run holds it (60- and 30-session annualised; there is no book price series, so no 1y book vol) and the book's return over exactly the same sessions (2026-06-10..09-04 spans the 60 daily returns; 07-24.. the 30) via book.explain_episode, then the ratio actually computed (return / annualised vol, both stated with their window); the 1y return and the run's max drawdown for the 'all year' framing. This is raw return per unit of vol — no risk-free rate, so not a Sharpe; VaR and expected shortfall are withheld on this desk.

W05-paid-for-the-vol#t2.note: the market's side of t1 over the same sessions: SPY's return 2026-06-10..09-04 from its own closes, its 63d vol (the nearest window to the run's 60d), its return per unit of vol, and the book's ratio over the market's (about 1.24x: the book earned more per unit of vol than owning the market over the stretch) plus the plain return ratio (book minus market is refused as mixed_worlds, so the excess is read off the two figures, _GAPS_A); the 1y pair as well.

W05-paid-for-the-vol#t3.note: name by name: each holding's 1y total return divided by its 252-session annualised vol over the same year, ranked lowest-first (TLT and MSFT negative, AMZN next); this is return per unit of vol, not Sharpe.

W06-is-that-all-of-them#t1.skip: filings text: customer-concentration language is read from each issuer's filing; no figure

W06-is-that-all-of-them#t2.skip: filings text: a coverage statement about which filings were opened; no figure

W06-weight-we-chose#t1.note: NVDA's weight on the latest run (2026-09-04) and the prior run (2026-09-03, one session earlier), NVDA's own return and the book's over that span, and the split: w_implied_prev = today's weight deflated by (1+r_book)/(1+r_i) is what yesterday's weight must have been if nothing was traded; drift = w - w_implied_prev is the market's part, chosen = w_implied_prev - w_prev is the part only a trade explains (both legs sum to w - w_prev). traded_dollars = mv - pnl - mv_prev is the same test in dollars (0 for NVDA: the whole move is drift). The desk has no blotter, so 'chosen' is an inference from the two snapshots, labelled as such. Built this way because prev-run x latest-run products are refused as different_books (_GAPS_A).

W06-weight-we-chose#t2.note: the same decomposition for all ten names between the two runs, ranked: drift highest-first says who is running away on price alone (one session only, so the drift is small everywhere), chosen and traded_dollars ranked show that nothing was traded (GOOGL's -$870 is the only non-zero, a rounding-scale residual). Same different_books construction as t1.

W06-weight-we-chose#t3.note: re-underwriting at today's 4.2% weight with what the desk holds: NVDA's revenue growth (yoy of 12-month total_revenues), operating margin over four years, FCF margin, distance from its 52w high, 63d vol, 1y beta/alpha/R² to SPY and 1y return vs SPY. Absent and said so: no valuation multiple (the desk has no valuation method), no entry price, no forecast — so 'would you put it on at this weight' is judged on business quality and risk, not on price.

FQ02-who-actually-buys-nvda#t3.skip: filings text: purchase obligations and supply commitments are a commitments-note disclosure, not a filed line

FQ03-is-aws-carrying-it#t1.note: Segment revenue and segment operating income are not held as figures (companyfacts are consolidated); the nearest held thing is the consolidated top line, operating income and operating margin, with the five-year margin series. The AWS share and the retail-versus-AWS split are stated as absent.

FQ03-is-aws-carrying-it#t2.skip: filings text: the segment discussion in their own words is MD&A prose

FQ03-is-aws-carrying-it#t3.note: Whether the consolidated whole is getting more or less profitable: operating margin over five fiscal years and eight quarters with the change in points over two years and year-on-year, net and FCF margins, operating income growth against revenue growth, and the position's weight so it lands on the book.

FQ04-their-story-against-my-line#t1.note: The computed line first, and the premise checked: NVDA gross margin over eight fiscal quarters with the move in points quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year (and the annual series), plus revenue, cost of revenue and gross profit quarterly with qoq so the answer can see which side moved. Management's stated reason is MD&A text and not in the program.

FQ04-their-story-against-my-line#t2.note: Sizes the move so their reason can be measured against it: the margin change in points is exactly the cost-of-revenue-to-revenue change; the dollar change in cost of revenue and revenue quarter-on-quarter and the inventory balance's move are the only held figures that bear on a provision story. The stated charge itself is text, so whether it covers the whole move is a netting the answer does with an absent figure named.

FQ04-their-story-against-my-line#t3.note: How much provisioning can move the number: the inventory balance over eight quarters, days inventory as a series, inventory against the quarter's cost of revenue, and a held sensitivity: one percent of the inventory balance expressed in gross-margin points of the quarter's revenue. The reserve balance, the period charge and management's own stated sensitivity are note text and are absent.

W01-useful-life-policy#t1.note: How much reported profit leans on the depreciation line: trailing-year depreciation over operating income (and over revenue) for MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, plus depreciation growth beside capex growth over four years (depreciation lagging capex is the fingerprint of a longer life). The policy passage, the years and the disclosed dollar effect are 10-K text and are not in the program. No vector can be formed from per-issuer scalars, so the ordering is read off the three dep_to_oi nodes, not a rank node.

W01-useful-life-policy#t2.note: Nearest computable restatement: operating margin now, less the change in depreciation-to-revenue between the fiscal year three years back (FY2023 for MSFT, 2022 for AMZN/GOOGL) and the trailing year: if the depreciation ratio went back to then, the margin moves by that many points. GOOGL's 2022 top line is read under the contract-revenue concept because total_revenues has no derivable 2022 window (window_not_derivable); the two differ only by non-contract income. The filing's own stated dollar effect of the life change is text and absent, and the ratio change also carries mix effects, which the answer must say.

W01-useful-life-policy#t3.note: The earliest tell of an over-stretched life is depreciation growing well below capex growth while capex-to-depreciation climbs: trailing capex over depreciation per name, depreciation-to-revenue, and the yoy of both series over four years. The level to worry at is a convention the answer names, not a mandate figure.

W01-xom-maturity-wall#t1.skip: filings text: the maturity schedule (per-year amounts, dates) lives only in the debt note; the desk holds no dated debt figures

W01-xom-maturity-wall#t2.skip: filings text: the fixed/floating split is a debt-note disclosure, not a filed line

W01-xom-maturity-wall#t3.note: Whether XOM's interest bill is already rising: quarterly interest expense with yoy and qoq, cash interest paid beside it, the trailing year against the prior trailing year, and total debt now versus a year ago so a rising bill can be tied to more debt or a higher rate; coverage over five years as context.

W01-xom-payout-plug#t1.note: Distributions against what the business generated on two frequencies: FCF, buybacks and dividends quarter by quarter over eight quarters (where a single quarter can be outspent) and over the trailing year (where the premise may fail), the trailing gap and the latest quarter's gap (read directly at months=3: a `latest` of the series cannot be combined by the typed calculator, see _GAPS_B.md), and the two plugs the balance sheet holds: cash's change and total debt's change over the year.

W01-xom-payout-plug#t2.note: Dividend cushion as a share of operating cash flow and of free cash flow over the trailing year, the same shares one year earlier, and the change; dividend and OCF quarterly yoy show which side is moving the share.

W01-xom-payout-plug#t3.note: What to watch on the next print: the latest quarter's dividend over that quarter's FCF as the watched ratio, with the quarterly FCF, OCF, capex (and its yoy), buybacks and cash balance series that would show a squeeze first. The trigger level is a convention the answer names.

W02-buyback-vs-dilution#t1.note: The count question answered from filed shares: MSFT shares outstanding at thirteen quarter-ends with period and yoy change and the three-year change, diluted weighted shares beside it, and the netting the question is about: trailing buybacks minus SBC, and SBC as a share of buybacks.

W02-buyback-vs-dilution#t2.note: Every issuer held (TLT/HYG are funds): share count yoy from the filed count (shares_outstanding where filed at quarter-ends; diluted weighted shares for NVDA/JPM/LLY where the point-in-time count is sparse), and SBC against buybacks with the net. Expected absences that are part of the answer: XOM files no sbc (metric_not_filed) so its net cannot be formed; AMZN's trailing buybacks are zero (none since 2024) so SBC-to-buybacks is division_by_zero and the count question there is answered by the share series alone. No cross-issuer vector can be formed from these scalars, so 'worst' is read off the eight yoy/ratio nodes, not a rank node (see _GAPS_B.md).

W02-buyback-vs-dilution#t3.note: The line is drawn on two held ratios: SBC as a share of buybacks (above 1 the count grows) and the share count's yoy sign, with SBC to revenue and to FCF for scale and SBC's own growth. The trim threshold is a convention the answer names.

W02-lly-coverage-trend#t1.note: Tests the 'barely any debt' premise with LLY total_debt, net debt and the leverage multiples, then EBIT interest coverage now and over five years with its yoy for the direction. The desk's net_debt_to_ebitda and debt_to_ebitda refuse at the latest window (input_unavailable: ebit needs interest_expense, which LLY stops filing after 2024-03-31; only interest_expense_nonoperating continues) and that refusal is part of the answer, so a calendar-2025 net-debt-to-EBITDA is rebuilt from pretax income + interest + D&A; the coverage method itself accepts the nonoperating line and settles.

W02-lly-coverage-trend#t2.note: The level is a convention the answer names against the held figures: coverage now and its five-year path, debt to operating cash flow, and the two things that move coverage (interest expense growth, debt growth). fcf_to_debt is expected to refuse for LLY (capex not filed after 2022-09-30) and is recorded as such.

W03-xom-trough-relever#t1.note: As-reported net-debt-to-EBITDA (and debt-to-EBITDA) first, then XOM's EBITDA over the five fiscal years held, the trough by `min` over the series, and today's net debt and total debt divided by it. The `min` node carries no period, so `at` on 2021-12-31 (the trough year in the held run; nothing earlier than FY2021 is filed) names the year with the same figure.

W03-xom-trough-relever#t2.skip: forecast: no crude-price sensitivity of EBITDA is held; the only computable anchor is t1's historical trough, already returned

W04-book-capex-hogs#t1.note: Capex intensity across all ten holdings as one vector ranked heaviest first (JPM not_applicable, LLY input_unavailable after 2022-09-30, TLT/HYG file nothing), capex as a share of operating cash flow per screenable issuer, FCF margin ranked lowest-first as the 'before anything comes back' view, and the book weights so the answer can size the hog. capex-to-OCF has no method, so it is six scalars, not a ranked vector.

W04-book-capex-hogs#t2.note: For the heaviest name by capex intensity (MSFT on the run's ranking): capex growth beside revenue and operating-cash-flow growth, annually and quarterly, capex intensity as a four-year series, and the CAGR gap.

W04-book-capex-hogs#t3.note: Concedes what the capex line misses: MSFT's operating lease liability now, a year ago, its change (the year's leased capacity added), that change against the cash capex line, and capex plus lease growth over OCF. Finance leases and unrecognised purchase commitments are note text and are not held as figures.

W04-growth-vs-margin-screen#t1.note: The screen over every screenable issuer: quarterly revenue with its yoy series (four points, so acceleration is visible) and gross margin now against the same quarter a year ago in points. gross_margin the method holds only for AAPL/MSFT/NVDA (gross_profit filed); GOOGL/AMZN/LLY file cost_of_revenue instead, so their margin is built as (revenue - cost of revenue)/revenue at two windows. XOM files neither gross_profit nor cost_of_revenue (input_unavailable) and JPM is a bank (not_applicable); TLT/HYG are funds. No cross-issuer vector exists for these scalars, so the worst-first order is read from the gm_chg nodes rather than a rank node.

W04-growth-vs-margin-screen#t2.note: The worst hit on t1's screen by margin points is MSFT (revenue yoy back up to 18.3% while gross margin is 1.1 points below a year ago; LLY is the other hit, -0.6 points). How big for us: MSFT's weight and market value on the latest run, its rank among positions and its room to the issuer-concentration warning. Whether the market has noticed: distance from the 52-week high, 3m/6m/1y returns relative to SPY, 12-1 momentum and the six-month drawdown depth. Carries t1's margin change and revenue yoy for MSFT so the follow-on stands alone.

W05-explain-the-day#t1.note: Book's return on the run day (exposure_metrics.daily_return) beside SPY's same-day return from two closes; book.reconcile splits it into the factor-explained sum and the alpha+residual, as shares. The run holds no per-position contribution table and book.explain_episode refuses a one-day window (insufficient_history), so contributions are rebuilt as weight x day-return for the five largest weights.

W05-explain-the-day#t2.note: The residual as a LEVEL on each of the last seven run days (book.reconcile on one completed run per as-of date: alpha_plus_residual beside the day's return; the share is unstable when the day's return is near zero, e.g. 09-02) plus the regression's own R-squared over its 750-session window, which is the standing unexplained fraction (1 - R2). No prior run is assumed: each run id is explicit.

W05-jpm-frame-breaks#t1.note: The half of the frame that works for a bank: dividends and buybacks over the trailing year against net income (payout), with their five-year series. The half that breaks, shown breaking, and those refusals are required content of the answer: capex is not filed (metric_not_filed) and free cash flow, FCF margin and capex intensity refuse as not_applicable; operating cash flow is returned but for a bank it is dominated by trading and deposit flows and is not a cash-generation measure.

W05-jpm-frame-breaks#t2.note: What the desk can watch instead of FCF for a bank: ROE (level and five years), ROA, the equity multiplier and equity-to-assets as the held leverage proxy, the payout ratio and what is retained, and equity's own growth. CET1, the stress capital buffer and the stress test are regulatory disclosures not held as figures; the level to worry at is named as a convention against the held ratios.

W05-leases-in-leverage#t1.note: Answers the definitional premise with figures: AMZN total_debt as the desk builds it (the balance sheet table shows which components it covers; operating_lease_liability_total is a separate filed line outside the cover), the lease liability beside it and as a share of debt, and debt-to-EBITDA as quoted versus with the lease liability added in.

W05-leases-in-leverage#t2.note: Debt-to-EBITDA without and with operating lease liabilities for AMZN, MSFT, AAPL, so the order can be compared. Expected refusals that are part of the answer: MSFT total_debt is incomplete_cover (commercial_paper last at 2025-06-30) so long_term_debt_total stands in; MSFT/AAPL ebitda refuse for want of a filed interest_expense in the window, so EBITDA is rebuilt as operating income + depreciation (+ amortization); AAPL's lease liability is last filed at 2025-09-27 (not_reported_at_this_date at 2026-03-28), so AAPL is read at that instant. The reorder is read off six scalars; no rank node is possible across issuers.

W05-leases-in-leverage#t3.note: Cash interest paid against interest expense booked for AMZN over the trailing year. AMZN files no interest_paid line at all (metric_not_filed, a required part of the answer) and its interest_expense concept ends 2024-03-31 (only interest_expense_nonoperating runs to 2026-03-31), so the cash-versus-book gap is stated as absent and the capitalised-interest question cannot be settled from figures.

W06-aapl-net-cash-buybacks#t1.note: Both legs of the netting at reader level: AAPL total_debt with its components (long-term debt incl. current maturities, commercial paper), cash and equivalents and quick assets, and net_debt with its sign. The interest_expense read is the cost of that gross debt, but AAPL stops filing the line after 2023-09-30, so the node settles on the last filed window (FY2023, as_of 2023-09-30), not the trailing year; the answer must date it.

W06-aapl-net-cash-buybacks#t2.skip: filings text: where the cash sits (jurisdiction, marketable securities mix) is 10-K prose, not a filed line

W06-aapl-net-cash-buybacks#t3.note: Tests 'borrowing to buy back' at the level co-movement can support: debt over eight quarters and its change over a year, cash's change, buybacks and dividends beside free cash flow quarterly and over the trailing year, and the self-funding gap (FCF minus distributions). A gap covered by cash drawdown or new debt is shown, but which dollar funded which is not a claim the figures license.

W06-nvda-buyback-timing#t1.note: Repurchase dollars in each of NVDA's last six fiscal quarters set beside where the stock traded: the adjusted close at each quarter-end and the quarter's return from the prior quarter-end (the desk has no average-price-in-quarter primitive), with today's distance from the 52-week high and one-year return for where those quarters sit on the path. 'Cheap' is a valuation call and no multiple is a measure here.

W06-nvda-buyback-timing#t2.note: The same test on AAPL: six fiscal quarters of repurchases beside the quarter-end adjusted close and each quarter's return, so steadiness of spend against price moves can be compared with NVDA's. Same limits: no in-quarter average price, no cheapness call.

W06-tax-rate-growth#t1.note: LLY's earnings composition over five fiscal years: revenue, pretax income, income tax and net income each with yoy, tax burden (net/pretax = 1 - effective rate) as a series, and the CAGR gap between net and pretax income as the growth the tax rate alone contributed. LLY files no operating_income line (metric_not_filed), so the operating layer is absent; the effective rate itself is read as 1 - tax_burden because series cannot be divided.

W06-tax-rate-growth#t2.note: No forecast: the counterfactual on realised years. With the tax burden held flat, net income can only grow at the pretax rate, so pretax CAGR (and the latest pretax yoy) is the growth that survives; the net-minus-pretax CAGR gap and the latest-year yoy gap are what the falling rate has been adding and would stop adding.
